gaps.text: In-line measurement of Product temperature with temperature sensor

Combining several spectroscopy methods (data fusion) (Low-level fusion of NIR diffuse reflection and MIR ATR is the later hypothesis, not the first test. Both probes must view the same product volume, data must be synchronised to a common time step, and each method needs its own calibration. The fused model must beat the best single method on held-out batches, otherwise the extra MIR channel is dropped.)
A product-specific calibration for this opaque concentrated milk product.
Accuracy, precision, detection limits or response time for fat and protein in this product.

items.finding: The source notes that temperature sensitivity of OH bands is a severe drawback for aqueous solutions in NIR and MIR, making tempered sample holders necessary.
items.how_it_applies: For an opaque concentrated milk product with high water content, this suggests temperature should be measured and controlled during in-line NIR measurement, and temperature variation should be included in testing.
items.limits_and_transfer_risks: This is a review statement from biopharmaceutical downstream processing, not a milk or in-line dairy study; tempered sample holders are a laboratory measure and may not transfer directly to a process line.

citation.quote: Additionally, the temperature sensitivity of the OH bands is a severe drawback for measuring aqueous solution in NIR and MIR, which makes tempered sample holders necessary [29].
citation.label: E01 ¶12

items.finding: The source varied temperature together with concentrations and ionic strength to obtain a robust model.
items.how_it_applies: This supports treating product temperature as a measured variable during calibration and robustness testing for the in-line NIR concept.
items.limits_and_transfer_risks: The work concerns reactive liquid-liquid extraction in lithium recycling, not milk or dairy processing; the temperature variation was part of model building rather than an in-line temperature-sensor study.

citation.quote: The concentrations of nitric acid and hydrochloric acid as well as the ionic strength and temperature were varied to obtain a robust model.
citation.label: E02 ¶19

items.finding: Before fusing data from multiple sources, the source says it is essential to evaluate each dataset's contribution to the model and its complementarity.
items.how_it_applies: For a later NIR plus MIR low-level fusion hypothesis, this suggests first checking whether the MIR data adds useful information beyond NIR before keeping the extra channel.
items.limits_and_transfer_risks: This is a review statement on data fusion in process analytical technology, not a milk-specific NIR/MIR study; it does not address same-volume viewing or time synchronisation.

citation.quote: Before fusing data from multiple sources, it is essential to evaluate the contribution of each dataset to the model and its complementarity.
citation.label: E03 ¶82

items.finding: The source reports situations where instrument complementarity alone was not sufficient to improve prediction of several CQAs in a Raman and FT-IR food analytical study.
items.how_it_applies: This cautions that adding MIR to NIR should be tested against the best single method on held-out batches rather than assumed to improve performance.
items.limits_and_transfer_risks: The cited example used Raman and FT-IR on food samples, not NIR diffuse reflection and MIR ATR on concentrated milk; laboratory results may not transfer to an in-line dairy process.

citation.quote: In some situations, instrument complementarity (not data complementarity) was not sufficient to improve the performance of predictive several CQAs, as shown by a Raman and FT-IR data based food analytical study [73].
citation.label: E03 ¶36

items.finding: For a continuous process at a fixed probe location operating in a steady-state window, the source says calibrations can be narrower and centered on the operational envelope, with validation using independent steady-state runs.
items.how_it_applies: This could inform a product-specific calibration strategy by defining the product and process operational envelope, using independent batches or runs for validation, and monitoring drift and out-of-specification conditions.
items.limits_and_transfer_risks: The source concerns reactive liquid-liquid extraction in lithium recycling, not an opaque concentrated milk product; the steady-state assumption and process behaviour may differ on a dairy line.

citation.quote: In contrast, a continuous process at a fixed probe location is intended to operate in a steady-state window, which simplifies the model design: calibrations can be narrower and centered on the operational envelope, validation can rely on independent steady-state runs, and online monitoring focuses on drift and out-of-specification detection rather than resolving the rapidly changing composition.
citation.label: E02 ¶8
